title: Part 3
html:
Through Orissa to Puri. Departure for the South. Meeting with Ramananda Raya. The Buddhists of Trimandal, Dhundhiram, the rich man Tirtharam (pp. 41–60)

[p. 41]

437Krishna is the truth beyond change, so say the Vedas;
he cannot be grasped by a changeful mind."

438Thus, having blessed many lands,
merciful Chaitanya hastened to Jaleshvar.

439At Jaleshvar there is a Shiva named Billeshvara;
seeing him, devotion welled up in the Lord's heart.

440A sannyasi lived in Shiva's temple,
and the Lord went slowly up to him.

441Coming before the sannyasi, he bowed down,
and the sannyasi, seeing the Lord, started.

442The sannyasi said, "Who are you? You are no ordinary man.
Why do you bow before me?

443By the fruit of what merit have I seen you today?
The moment I saw you, my bonds were cut.

444You are the fruit of my austerities, O merciful one;
seeing you, all my sins have been destroyed."

445Thus the excellent sannyasi, gazing at the Lord,
choked with love and burst into tears.

446At once my Lord, to hide his identity,
raised his arms and began to dance, crying "Hari!"

447Now crying "Krishna!" he leaps and runs,
now falls to the ground and rolls about.

[p. 42]

448A great crowd gathered for the sankirtana of the Name,
and my Chaitanya passed the night awake.

449Next day, coming to the bank of the Suvarnarekha,
he was thrilled to see Raghunatha Dasa.1

450Then we went on to Hariharpur,
and there Nimai became intoxicated with the Name of Hari.

451He fell crashing to the ground,
[the second line of the couplet is missing in the edition]

452and so that day passed,
the Lord weeping, drunk with bliss.

453The next day we went to Baleshvar;
seeing Gopala, the Lord was in great bliss.

454Next morning we went to Nilagarh,
and at Nilagarh Nimai became drunk with the Name.

455As he danced, he gradually lost consciousness
and fell crashing to the ground.

456Thus that day passed;
countless onlookers came and sat around him.

457As he sang the Name his bliss increased,
and the Lord fell senseless to the ground.

458Thus the devotees gathered together
and became intoxicated, tasting supreme bliss.

459Next day, coming to the bank of the river Vaitarani,
he burst into tears, crying, "Krishna, take me across!"2

[p. 43]

460His body choked with love, always as if crazed,
he walks on saying "Hari", looking neither right nor left.

461The next day we crossed the Mahanadi,
and on the way we saw the deity Gopinatha.

462We all received Gopinatha's maha-prasada,
and with that prasada joy surged in our hearts.

463Then, all filled with love,
we set off to see Sakshi-Gopala.3

464Raising his arms and crying "Hari!", he began to run,
and his falling tears turned the earth to mud.

465Seeing Sakshi-Gopala from afar,
he sprawled on the ground, choked with love.

466Seeing Gopala, it was as if he remembered something,
and at once, gazing at his face, he began to weep.

467"Gopala, Gopala!" he called again and again.
Who can describe the force of his love?

468Then, going to the temple of Lingaraja,
the Lord burst into tears in some mood unknown.4

469Leaving Lingaraja we came to Atharanala;5
seeing the temple flag, my Lord fell to the ground.

470Never had I seen such a flood of tears:
[p. 44]
the Lord turned the earth to mud with the stream of his tears.

471Crying, "Ah, ah, Lord Jagannatha!", Sri Hari
flooded the ground, shedding tears.

472He falls and flails and weeps aloud;
whoever he sees before him he clasps in his arms.

473"Look, there is my Krishna dancing as a cowherd boy!
Ah, how beautiful his hair is!"

474Seeing the Lord's temple he weeps aloud,
now and then falling crashing to the ground.

475He rushed to the Lord's door and rolled in the dust,
but for the stream of his tears he could not see Vishnu's form.

476Falling, flailing, crying out, rolling on the ground —
a hundred thousand people came to see that state.

477With great difficulty the Lord checked the flow of his love,
but on seeing Mahavishnu he burst into tears again.

478The devotees were startled by the sound of his weeping,
and he ran and embraced Gadadhara.

479He went to the Garuda pillar and clung to it;
his forehead was cut and blood began to flow.

480Seeing this, [illegible]6 with his upper cloth
wiped the Lord's blood away.

481Having had darshan, he went to Mishra's house,7
and the devotees began to arrive in procession.

[p. 45]

482Thus, staying some time in Puri,
we enjoyed ever new delights each day.

483The Avadhuta, Krishnadasa and Haridasa
stayed by the Lord, relishing supreme bliss.

484Puri was filled with the sound of the Name all eight watches,8
and everyone rolled on the ground.

485Some string garlands, some grind sandalwood,
some prepare the bhoga offering.

486Gradually all the companions gathered,
and Puri's splendour surpassed Vaikuntha.

487The brahmana Krishnadasa and pot-bellied Shyamadasa
guard the Lord on either side.

488Now he falls, drunk with love,
now he leaps into the sea.

489Premadasa, Gopadasa and the brahmana mahanta
shower nectar, reading the Bhagavata.

490Raghunatha Dasa and Acharya Shekhara,
Damodara, Narahari and Gadadhara —

491every day all of them go together to the holy temple,
taking my Lord along in their midst.

492Sweet mridangas play, sometimes kartals too;
he is always drunk with the Name, with no thought of time.

[p. 46]

493Thus my Lord, in Mishra's house,
was always rejoicing with the devotees.

494Every day Kashi Mishra brings prasada,9
its fragrance stealing the heart, its taste sweet.

495All kinds of fried and roasted dishes — how many!
How much prasada I stuffed into my belly!

496Fried chickpeas, crunchy mixtures, mung, beans,
sesame, linseed, wheat and barley — I would die for them!

497Hundreds of fruits and roots, scraped coconut —
every day the Gora of Nadia gives them to me with his own hands.

498Sugar crystals, dates, laddus and gaja,
adhasa, pitha, puli, juicy gaja,

499rice soaked in ghee, bhuta-ghonto, nota greens —
after eating such prasada I am lost for words.

500Speechless, every day I eat my fill;
whatever I get goes straight into my belly.

501Thus the days went by,
and gradually all the devotees began to arrive.

502Shankara Bharati and Paramananda Puri,
Damodara Svami, Pradyumna Brahmachari,

503Chidananda Giri, Premananda Sarasvati
came and went to the Lord every day.

[p. 47]

504Many devotees gathered together at Nilachala
and worshipped with great delight.

505At this time Sarvabhauma appeared,
and with him many devotees came and joined them.

506Seeing Mahavishnu, the Lord was filled with longing
and bowed again and again in devotion.

507Seeing Govinda,10 the Lord fainted
and lay there like a corpse.

508Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya was there;
he lifted him in his arms and carried him to his own house.

509How much service he rendered the Lord!
The rasa of devotion overflowed in Sarvabhauma.

510Then, having given devotion to Sarvabhauma,
the Lord made ready to set out on his southern journey.

511For three months my Chaitanya Gosai
stayed in Puri together with Nitai.

512Then, on the seventh day of Vaishakha,
he set out for the South, floating in the nectar of love.

513At the time of departure Nitai grew anxious
and, humbled by devotion, began to speak:

514"Do not go alone," said Nityananda Raya;
"let all of us go along with you."

[p. 48]

515Very eager to go was Gadadhara, dear as his own life,
and Premananda Sarasvati and Shankara Bharati.

516Hearing this, my Lord smiled a little
and said, "I shall go alone, without companions."

517The Avadhuta Nityananda, hearing these words,
began to speak, shedding tears:

518"You are going far away to the South.
Let the brahmana Krishnadasa Thakura go with you.

519The brahmana is pure and will do
whatever you tell him to do."

520"How can we stay here without you?
That is why we all say: let us go with you."

521Hearing this, Mahaprabhu smiled a little
and, giving them instructions, dissuaded them all.

522Hearing that, they all said,
"Then let your servant Govinda go with you."

523Hearing this, my Lord said, smiling,
"I am very fond of Govinda's company.

524Whoever goes or does not go, Govinda will go;
whatever work I have, Govinda will do."11

525Saying this, Sri Chaitanya took his leave
and set off southwards, all the devotees running after him.

[p. 49]

526Little by little, very slowly,
we all reached the temple of Alalanatha.

527Seeing Alalanatha, his feelings overflowed,
and he soaked the earth of that place with his tears.

528Dancing, the Lord lost consciousness
and fell crashing to the ground.

529Next morning, taking leave of everyone,
we three set out on our southern journey.12

530At this time Sarvabhauma said softly:
"On the bank of the Godavari you will meet Raya.

531Ramananda Raya is the best of devotees who know rasa;
at Krishna's name his eyes are always wet with tears.

532Rama Raya enjoys pure bliss;
at the Name of Hari his heart rejoices."

533Hearing this, he hastened to the bank of the Godavari,
and there Ramananda came and met him.

534Seeing the young sannyasi, devotion arose in him;
Rama Raya clasped his feet and began to weep.

535Ramananda Raya said, "You are God himself.
I am most fortunate to have seen you."

536The Lord said, "Raya, speak about Krishna;
by your conclusions the ache of my heart will go."

[p. 50]

537Raya said, "Lord, I know nothing;
unless you make me speak, no words will come."

538"Dwelling in the heart, you teach everything;
by your mercy you make the dumb eloquent."

539The Lord asked, "By what truth is the mind purified?"
Raya said, "That truth is meeting with the saints."

540"I want from you a truth subtler still."
Raya said, "There is no truth beyond renunciation."

541The Lord said, "The subtle truth is attachment to God."
Raya said, "Higher even than that is prema-bhakti."

542The Lord said, "Tell me a deeper essence still, O wise one."
Raya said, "The essence of all is Rai, full of rasa."13

543Rama Raya wanted to tell a deeper essence still,
but Gora Raya at once covered his mouth.

544The Lord said, "Butter lies hidden in milk;
he who churns will get its taste."

545The Lord said, "Raya, I know nothing.
Speak, speak of Krishna; let me hear it from your mouth.

546You, Rama Raya, are a Vaishnava detached from the world.
Speak, speak the truth of Krishna, let my heart be soothed."

547Hearing the Lord's words, Ramananda Raya
folded his hands in humility and said:

[p. 51]

548"Why do you play tricks again and again, Lord of the universe?
Be merciful and make this servant your follower.

549You have spread the rasa of devotion all over the land
and in your mercy sanctified this earth.

550Have mercy on this wretched one, Jagannatha;
give detachment to my heart and take me with you."

551Hearing this, the Lord embraced Raya,
and Rama Raya, clasping his knees, wept.

552Ramananda's breast was flooded with tears,
and seeing this the Lord said in a choked voice:

553"You, Rama Raya, are the crest-jewel of Vaishnavas."
Ramananda, his face lowered, kept saying "Rama, Rama".

554The Lord said, "Raya, you are most fortunate;
your devotion is beyond description."

555Raya said, "I am the lowest of sinners;
you have been defiled by touching me.

556Mercifully forgive me that offence,
and, seated in my heart, make me taste devotion."

557That night Ramananda passed
in such conversation with Gora-chand.

558Next day Raya clasped the Lord's feet,
[p. 52]
took his leave and went off to his own duties.

559The Lord said, "Ramananda, now I shall go on;
come to Nilachala and stay with me.

560You, I and the Bhatta14 will live in seclusion
and, discussing the truth of Krishna, find peace in life."

561So saying, the Lord sent Raya away,
and Ramananda bowed and went home.

562Of all that Raya said with the Lord,
not a hundredth part has remained in this book.

563Thus Ramananda came for ten days
and rejoiced to see the sannyasi of Nadia.

564The Lord felt great affection on seeing Ramananda,
and Raya lost consciousness on seeing the Lord.

565Taking leave of Raya,
the Lord entered the town of Trimandal.15

566Many Buddhists live in the town of Trimandal;
they all came to meet beautiful Gauranga.

567The Lord debated with the Buddhists,
and the king of Trimandal came to act as arbiter.

568The Buddhists admitted defeat in the debate,
and all the pandits and onlookers burst out laughing.

569All said, "This sannyasi is no man!
The way he debated is beyond words."

[p. 53]

570The chief of the Buddhists, Ramagiri Raya,
bowed and said, "Show me the way.

571You are no man, young sannyasi;
I long to stay with you.

572In the world I was the crest-jewel of unbelievers;
mercifully show me the path of devotion."

573Smiling, Lord Chaitanya said kindly:
"You are my master, Ramagiri Raya.

574One who thrills with joy saying 'Hari'
is my master — that is the practice."

575Hearing the Lord's words, Ramagiri Raya
at once fell crashing to the ground.

576Lying at his feet, Ramagiri said,
"What have you said to this lowest of men, O merciful one?

577Dwelling in all beings, you see everything.
Mercifully give me a place at your crimson feet."

578Devotion arose in Ramagiri the unbeliever,
and seeing this my Lord was filled with joy.

579All the Buddhists, crest-jewels of pandits,
followed Ramagiri's path.

580The young sannyasi left the disputants without hope;
seeing this, Ramananda16 looked all around.

[p. 54]

581At last, eager to debate,
came Dhundhiram Tirtha, who lived by the Tungabhadra.

582Ever drunk with pride, vain of his learning,
he did not understand the path of devotion — learned only in dry logic.

583Dhundhiram was indeed a great pandit,
but he was very much afraid of debating.

584Svami Dhundhiram went to debate,
but the Lord, shedding tears, rolled on the ground again and again.

585The Lord said, "Listen, listen, Svami Dhundhiram:
I have lost the argument with you.

586I will write you a certificate of victory in secret:
'Chaitanya has now lost to you.'

587By the grace of Vani17 you are a learned Gosai;
who could beat you in logic and scripture?

588Nyaya, Sankhya, Patanjala and Vedanta —
you are expert in every shastra, good sir.

589I am an ignorant sannyasi and know nothing;
again and again I admit defeat before you.

590You are more learned than the Dhundhi of old;18
your learning is famous throughout the world."

591So saying, he sent Dhundhiram away,
but Dhundhi did not want to go and looked all around.

[p. 55]

592After looking this way and that, Dhundhi
fell at the Lord's feet with a heart made wholly pure.

593Having given devotion to the unbeliever Dhundhi,
the Lord set out for Pantha-guha, remembering Sri Hari.19

594Dhundhiram became known by the name Haridasa,
and the unbelievers whispered and said all sorts of things.

595Smiling, the Lord called me,
and I lifted the two pairs of sandals onto my shoulders.

596The sandals, water-pot and whatever belongings we had,
and also what Raya had given, I gathered up and took.

597Not far away there was a banyan called Akshaya;
at dusk the Lord arrived at that place.

598A Shiva named Vateshvara is there,
and Gora-chand hastened there with devotion.

599With devotion the Lord bowed to Vateshvara
and spent the night there without food.

600In the morning the Lord went to bathe,
and I went from door to door begging alms.

601I came back with the alms at midday;
my Gora Raya cooked and made the offering.

602I received prasada like nectar,
and just then the wealthy Tirtha20 arrived.

[p. 56]

603Two harlots came with him to look,
to test the sannyasi's vaunted firmness.

604The harlots named Satyabai and Lakshmibai
came up to the Lord and talked of many things.

605Coached by Tirtha, those two harlots
made many attempts to see through the Lord.

606Tirtharam said all sorts of things to himself:
"Now by a trick I will rob this sannyasi of his power."

607Lakshmi played all manner of tricks, and Satyabala laughed;
Satyabala sat down beside the Lord with a smile.

608Satya undid her bodice and bared her breasts,
and the Lord addressed Satya as "Mother".

609At the Lord's words Satya trembled all over,
and seeing this Lakshmi was much afraid.

610There was not the slightest agitation in the Lord's mind.
Satyabala ran and fell at his feet.

611"Why do you make me an offender, Mother?"
Saying only this, the Lord fell to the ground.

612His matted hair came loose, he was grey with dust,
his body trembling all over with longing.

613Everything about my Lord was in disarray;
he no longer saw where Lakshmi was, where Satya was.

[p. 57]

614Saying "Hari, Hari!" the Lord began to dance,
his hair standing on end, tears streaming down.

615His kaupina had slipped off; where was his outer cloth?
He danced naked, breathing hard and fast.

616He falls, heedless of thorns and splinters;
the bunch of garlands at his neck has broken.

617From fasting he is nothing but skin and bone;
streams of blood flow over his thin limbs.

618Drunk with the Name of Hari, Gora Raya dances,
and a wondrous radiance comes forth from his body.

619Seeing this, that rich man was shaken within;
he fell at his feet and took refuge.

620The Lord, unaware of the outer world, tramples him underfoot;
crying "Hari!" with arms upraised he dances onwards.

621Clasping Satya in his arms he says, "Say 'Hari'!
Say 'Hari', lord of life, Mukunda, Murari!"

622Where is the Lord, where is Mukunda-Murari?
Seeing such a state, all lost consciousness.

623Drunk with the Name of Hari, the Lord has no outer awareness;
his head droops, his soul in turmoil.

624Froth at his mouth, dust on his limbs, no cloth,
his hair bristling, his eyes closed.

[p. 58]

625Seeing this state, all the Buddhists cry, "Hari, Hari!"
Hearing it, tears flow from Gora's eyes.

626The tears began to spurt like a squirt-gun;
seeing this, Tirtharam burst into tears.

627"I am a great unbeliever," says Tirtharam;
"be merciful, Lord, and give me the Name of Hari."

628Embracing the unbeliever Tirtharam,
the Lord says, "Tirtharam, you are a holy man.

629I have been purified by touching you.
'You are a foremost devotee,'" he says again and again.

630Then the rich Tirtharam fell at his feet
and wept long in great distress.

631When, through his weeping, devotion arose,
the Lord at once took his hand and embraced him.

632The Lord said, "Count riches as straw,
and then you will gain the priceless jewel of devotion.

633Throw your clothes and ornaments far away;
leave transient wealth and worship the eternal treasure.

634Coming and going again and again you will suffer —
this is the counsel for those free from desire.

635This cherished body, covered with skin,
will rot in a few days' time.

[p. 59]

636When the bird of life flies from the body,
it becomes either worms, or ashes, or excrement.

637In the three worlds there is nothing to be proud of;
the only glory lies in worshipping God.

638Knowing luxury and wealth to be transient,
throw them away one by one.

639Faith in God brings God to you;
no other proof can be put into words.

640Countless worlds are proof of it,
yet the learned gosai wants proof.

641There is no need for much debate and wrangling;
Krishna comes and meets the seeker through faith.

642What need is there to discuss many shastras?
Have faith and worship Krishna.

643One who boasts of wealth again and again
suffers unceasing sorrow day by day.

644One who prides himself for the sake of honour —
tell me, who will relieve his sorrow?

645'This is mine, I am his' — so everyone says,
but when the eyes close, no one belongs to anyone.

646All people pretend to kinship for nothing;
mourning a dead body is like mourning a broken doll.

[p. 60]

647The son is born of the father, everyone knows,
but the Vedas do not teach that the two minds are one.

648When life leaves the son's body,
that does not mean the father dies.

649The son takes birth from the mother's body,
but know for certain that the two are not one.

650No one belongs to anyone — this is the course of what is to be known,
and it cannot be established by proofs.

651God is the object of knowledge, and the proof of him
is present within the human heart.

652Fools think him farther than the far;
the wise accept that he is very near.

653I have told you the essence of truth, the teaching of the Vedas;
foolish people do not seek it.

654Whoever knows all these true principles
does not die again and again."

655Hearing all this from the Lord's lips, Tirtharam
gave up attachment to worldly things and chanted the Name of Hari.

656The Lord became intoxicated with the sankirtana of Hari,
and gradually his companions came and gathered round.21

657"The rich Tirtharam has fallen into trouble" —
so the unbelievers said of him, gossiping in many ways.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Raghunatha Dasa (Gosvami) of Saptagram fled to Chaitanya at Puri only some years later. A meeting at the Suvarnarekha in 1510 is one of the details of the Karcha that critics regard as anachronistic.
  2. The Vaitarani is a real river in Orissa and also the mythical river at the border of Yama's realm which must be "crossed"; hence the double sense of the cry.
  3. Sakshi-Gopala, "Gopala the witness", is a deity near Puri. Gopinatha, mentioned just before, is on the traditional route at Remuna (near Baleshvar), not after the Mahanadi; Govinda may have confused the order.
  4. Lingaraja is the chief Shiva temple of Bhubaneswar.
  5. Atharanala is the eighteen-arched stone bridge at the entrance to Puri, from which the flag of Jagannatha's temple is first seen.
  6. The word is corrupt in the edition (dhyanapura); perhaps the name of one of the companions.
  7. Kashi Mishra, in whose house Chaitanya later lived in Puri.
  8. The eight watches (at-pahar): round the clock.
  9. The beginning of this line is partly lost in the edition and is restored from the sense.
  10. Probably Jagannatha, whom Govinda here calls Govinda; possibly a separate deity of the temple complex.
  11. A key passage for the controversy. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 7) only the brahmana Krishnadasa went south with Chaitanya. The Karcha acknowledges Krishnadasa's candidacy but asserts that Govinda went too.
  12. "We three": Chaitanya, Govinda and apparently Krishnadasa, who is hardly mentioned afterwards.
  13. Rai is Radha. A compressed version of the famous dialogue of Chaitanya and Ramananda (CC Madhya 8), structured quite differently from the Charitamrita.
  14. Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya.
  15. Trimandal (Trimanda) is a place near the Godavari, perhaps Trimalgiri or Tirumalla in Sen's reading; the identification is uncertain.
  16. So in the edition; perhaps Ramagiri is meant.
  17. Vani is Sarasvati, goddess of learning.
  18. An allusion to some famous Dhundhi of the past, probably a commentator.
  19. Pantha-guha, "the traveller's cave", is a place-name; cf. the robber Pantha Bhil in the next part.
  20. Tirtharam, the rich man of the following episode.
  21. The line is unclear; perhaps Tirtharam's companions are meant.
